sentences.text:
1
 The Hon'Ble Smt. Justice Tirumala Devi Eada
 Criminal Petition No.14416 Of 2025
 Order:

This Criminal Petition is filed by the petitioners - accused Nos.2 to 5 seeking to quash the charge sheet in C.C.No.3912 of 2024 on the file of the learned VII Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate at Nampally, Hyderabad District, registered for the offences under Sections 420 and 406 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860.

entities.text: VII Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate at Nampally, Hyderabad District
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
2. Heard Ms.R.Leela Alekya, learned counsel representing Sri Shiva Kumar Konne, learned counsel for the petitioners and Sri Jithender Rao Veeramalla, learned Additional Public Prosecutor for respondent No.1 - State.
3.
Learned counsel for the petitioners submitted that the petitioners herein are arrayed as Accused Nos. 2 to 5 and are facing false allegations under Sections 420 and 406 of the IPC.

She further submitted that the alleged transactions between the petitioners and the de facto complainant pertain to certain land dealings, and it is alleged that the petitioners received advance sale consideration for registering the land in favour of the de facto complainant.
However, such allegations do not attract the offences punishable under Sections 420 and 406 of the IPC.

She further submitted that a Memorandum of Understanding was also entered into between the parties,
and by virtue of the same, the present case was agreed to be withdrawn.
However, the de facto complainant has not yet withdrawn the present case.
Hence, she prayed to quash the proceedings against the petitioners.

4. On the other hand, the learned Additional Public Prosecutor submitted that the allegations against the petitioners are that they received the sale consideration from the de facto complainant on the pretext of selling the land, but instead, the petitioners sold the said land to a third party and failed to register it in the name of the de facto complainant.
Hence, he prayed to dismiss the petition.
5. Perused the record.
The contents of the complaint and the recitals of the charge sheet disclose specific allegations constituting the offences under Sections 406 and 420 of the IPC.
The Memorandum of Understanding relied upon by the petitioners reveals the names of the de facto complainant and petitioner No.1, and certain terms and conditions were entered into between them.
However, it is not known whether those conditions were complied with, particularly regarding the return of the amounts in the event the present case was to be withdrawn.

6.
Accordingly, the criminal petition is disposed of.
7. As a sequel, the miscellaneous petitions pending, if any, shall stand closed.
